name: Serpent column
_about: THE SERPENT COLUMN of a Maya-Toltec temple door (Chichen Itza, Tula): the feathered serpent standing on its head -- the HEAD on the floor, jaws open toward the approach (+z), the BODY rising out of its skull as the square shaft, and the TAIL bent forward at the top as the capital, its rattle carrying the lintel. `W` the head's width (the shaft is four fifths of it), `H` the column's whole height, floor to the lintel's soffit.

body._about: the serpent's body, the shaft, rising out of its skull

tail._about: the tail bent forward over the door, its rattle the capital under the lintel
